lookback_source.quote: The standard look-back period for the MDS 3.0 is 7 days, unless otherwise stated.

lookback_notes: The D0150 pages do not state a numeric assessor observation/look-back window for this item; the 7-day value comes from the general convention (p. 3-3, standard MDS 3.0 look-back is 7 days unless otherwise stated), counted as the ARD plus the 6 previous calendar days (p. 2-21). The item's own pages state only that the interview is conducted during the look-back period of the ARD (p. D-2) and that if the resident interview was not conducted within the look-back period of the ARD, D0100 must be coded 1 and dashes entered in the resident interview items (p. D-3). Separately, the interview questions themselves use a 14-day (2-week) symptom-recall period ("Over the last 2 weeks, have you been bothered by any of the following problems?", p. D-3; frequency codes span 0–14 days, p. D-6); this is a symptom-recall period inside the interview questions, not the assessor observation window. The coexistence of the two windows is recorded in conflicts.

coding_levels.label: Column 1, Symptom Presence — No

source.quote: Code 0, no: if resident indicates symptoms listed are not present. Enter 0 in Column 2 as well.

coding_levels.label: Column 1, Symptom Presence — Yes
coding_levels.definition: Resident indicates symptoms listed are present. Enter 0, 1, 2, or 3 in Column 2, Symptom Frequency.

source.quote: Code 1, yes: if resident indicates symptoms listed are present. Enter 0, 1, 2, or 3 in Column 2, Symptom Frequency.

coding_levels.label: Column 1, Symptom Presence — No response
coding_levels.definition: Resident was unable or chose not to complete the assessment or responded nonsensically. Leave Column 2, Symptom Frequency, blank.

source.quote: Code 9, no response: if the resident was unable or chose not to complete the assessment or responded nonsensically. Leave Column 2, Symptom Frequency, blank.

coding_levels.label: Column 1, Symptom Presence — Dash
coding_levels.definition: Enter a dash in Column 1 if the symptom presence was not assessed.

source.quote: Enter a Dash in Column 1 if the symptom presence was not assessed.

coding_levels.label: Column 2, Symptom Frequency — Never or 1 day
coding_levels.definition: Resident indicates that during the past 2 weeks they have never been bothered by the symptom or have only been bothered by the symptom on 1 day.

source.quote: Code 0, never or 1 day: if the resident indicates that during the past 2 weeks they have never been bothered by the symptom or have only been bothered by the symptom on 1 day.

coding_levels.label: Column 2, Symptom Frequency — 2-6 days (several days)
coding_levels.definition: Resident indicates that during the past 2 weeks they have been bothered by the symptom for 2-6 days.

source.quote: Code 1, 2-6 days (several days): if the resident indicates that during the past 2 weeks they have been bothered by the symptom for 2-6 days.

coding_levels.label: Column 2, Symptom Frequency — 7-11 days (half or more of the days)
coding_levels.definition: Resident indicates during the past 2 weeks they have been bothered by the symptom for 7-11 days.

source.quote: Code 2, 7-11 days (half or more of the days): if the resident indicates during the past 2 weeks they have been bothered by the symptom for 7-11 days.

coding_levels.label: Column 2, Symptom Frequency — 12-14 days (nearly every day)
coding_levels.definition: Resident indicates during the past 2 weeks they have been bothered by the symptom for 12-14 days.

source.quote: Code 3, 12-14 days (nearly every day): if the resident indicates during the past 2 weeks they have been bothered by the symptom for 12-14 days.

coding_levels.label: Column 2, Symptom Frequency — Dash
coding_levels.definition: In the rare situation that the resident cannot provide a frequency following a yes response in Column 1, enter a dash in Column 2; CMS expects a dash response to be rare.

source.quote: In the rare situation that the resident cannot provide a frequency, following a yes response to a symptom in Column 1, enter a dash in Column 2. CMS expects a dash response to be rare.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Conduct the Resident Mood Interview for any resident when D0100 = 1.

source.quote: Interview any resident when D0100 = 1.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Attempt to conduct the interview with ALL residents.

source.quote: Attempt to conduct the interview with ALL residents.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Read each item as it is written and do not provide definitions; the item is scored based on the resident's own interpretation of the wording.

source.quote: Do not provide definitions because the meaning must be based on the resident's interpretation.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Each question must be asked in sequence to assess Symptom Presence (Column 1) and Symptom Frequency (Column 2) before proceeding to the next question.

source.quote: Each question must be asked in sequence to assess Symptom Presence (column 1) and Symptom Frequency (column 2) before proceeding to the next question.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Enter code 9 in Column 1 and leave Column 2 blank if the resident was unable or chose not to complete the assessment or responded nonsensically (unrelated, incomprehensible, incoherent, or not informative for the item being rated).

source.quote: Enter code 9 in Column 1 and leave Column 2 blank if the resident was unable or chose not to complete the assessment or responded nonsensically.

federal_coding_rules.rule: For a yes response, ask the resident how often they were bothered by the symptom over the last 2 weeks, using the D0150 Column 2 Symptom Frequency response choices and the cue card categories.

source.quote: For a yes response, ask the resident to tell you how often they were bothered by the symptom over the last 2 weeks.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Gateway rule: if both D0150A1 and D0150B1 are coded 9, OR both D0150A2 and D0150B2 are coded 0 or 1, end the PHQ interview; otherwise continue with the remaining seven questions.

source.quote: If both D0150A1 and D0150B1 are coded 9, OR both D0150A2 and D0150B2 are coded 0 or 1, end the PHQ interview; otherwise continue.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If both D0150A1 and D0150B1 are coded 9, leave D0150A2 and D0150B2 blank, end the PHQ-2©, leave D0160 Total Severity Score blank, and skip to D0700, Social Isolation.

source.quote: If both D0150A1 and D0150B1 are coded 9, leave D0150A2 and D0150B2 blank, then end the PHQ-2©, leave D0160, Total Severity Score blank, and skip to D0700, Social Isolation.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If both D0150A2 and D0150B2 are coded 0 or 1, end the PHQ-2© and enter the total score from D0150A2 and D0150B2 in D0160, Total Severity Score.

source.quote: If both D0150A2 and D0150B2 are coded 0 or 1, then end the PHQ-2© and enter the total score from D0150A2 and D0150B2 in D0160, Total Severity Score.

federal_coding_rules.rule: For all other scenarios, proceed to ask the remaining seven questions (D0150C to D0150I of the PHQ-9©) and complete D0160, Total Severity Score.

source.quote: For all other scenarios, proceed to ask the remaining seven questions (D0150C to D0150I of the PHQ-9©) and complete D0160, Total Severity Score.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Record the resident's responses as they are stated, regardless of whether the resident or the assessor attributes the symptom to something other than mood.

source.quote: Record the resident's responses as they are stated, regardless of whether the resident or the assessor attributes the symptom to something other than mood.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If Column 1 equals 0, enter 0 in Column 2.

source.quote: If Column 1 equals 0, enter 0 in Column 2.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If Column 1 equals 9 or dash, leave Column 2 blank.

source.quote: If Column 1 equals 9 or dash, leave Column 2 blank.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Select only one frequency response per item.

source.quote: Select only one frequency response per item.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If the resident has difficulty selecting between two frequency responses, code for the higher frequency.

source.quote: If the resident has difficulty selecting between two frequency responses, code for the higher frequency.

federal_coding_rules.rule: For items containing more than one phrase (e.g., D0150F), if the resident gives different frequencies for different parts of a single item, select the highest frequency as the score for that item.

source.quote: Some items (e.g., item D0150F) contain more than one phrase. If a resident gives different frequencies for the different parts of a single item, select the highest frequency as the score for that item.

federal_coding_rules.rule: In the rare situation that the resident cannot provide a frequency following a yes response in Column 1, enter a dash in Column 2.

source.quote: In the rare situation that the resident cannot provide a frequency, following a yes response to a symptom in Column 1, enter a dash in Column 2.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If the resident interview was not conducted within the look-back period of the ARD, item D0100 must be coded 1, Yes, and the standard "no information" code (a dash "-") entered in the resident interview items.

source.quote: If the resident interview was not conducted within the look-back period of the ARD, item D0100 must be coded 1, Yes, and the standard "no information" code (a dash "-") entered in the resident interview items.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Resident refusal or unwillingness to participate in the interview results in D0100 being coded 1, Yes, and code 9, No response, being entered in Column 1, Symptom Presence; assessors then proceed to D0700, Social Isolation.

source.quote: Resident refusal or unwillingness to participate in the interview would result in Item D0100 being coded 1, Yes, and code 9, No response being entered in Column 1. Symptom Presence.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Conduct the interview in a private setting; if an interpreter is used, the interpreter should not attempt to determine the intent behind what is being translated, the outcome of the interview, or the meaning or significance of the resident's responses.

source.quote: If an interpreter is used during resident interviews, the interpreter should not attempt to determine the intent behind what is being translated, the outcome of the interview, or the meaning or significance of the resident's responses.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The D0150 pages do not tie this item to any payment or case-mix classification.

conflicts.topic: Which time window governs D0150: the ARD look-back period for conducting the interview vs. the 2-week symptom recall period inside the interview questions

positions.claim: The Resident Mood Interview is conducted during the look-back period of the ARD (no number of days stated on the item's pages), and the standard MDS 3.0 look-back is 7 days unless otherwise stated.

source.quote: This interview is conducted during the look-back period of the Assessment Reference Date (ARD) and is not contingent upon item B0700, Makes Self Understood.

positions.claim: The interview questions and all frequency codes reference symptoms over the last 2 weeks (up to 14 days), a longer recall period than the standard 7-day observation window.

source.quote: Say to resident: "Over the last 2 weeks, have you been bothered by any of the following problems?"

conflicts.resolution: unresolved — surface to user. Recorded as: assessor observation window = 7 days per general convention (p. 3-3); symptom-recall window inside the interview = last 2 weeks per the item's own pages.

not_found: lookback_days (not stated on the item's own pages; supplied by general convention p. 3-3)
